note: Anchoring capability adopted. Manifest anchor-0001 commits the ledger through ev-000014, the registry tree, and the measured roadmap status. Recorded after the manifest, necessarily: a manifest cannot commit the hash of a ledger that already contains the event describing it. Status is ANCHOR_PENDING — the OpenTimestamps client is not yet installed, so the digest is fixed but not yet submitted to a calendar server.

Model revision: split the coordinate vector into three layers (coordinates, governance intent, functions). Opened as a separate proposal rather than folded into OTCS-0002, whose subject is unrelated; bundling would force anyone objecting to one to object to both. 45-day floor, earliest ratification 2026-09-10.

relationship.schema.json gains otcs_observed status, non_claims and observed_source. Until now a one-sided registry observation about projects that had not consented was unrecordable: additionalProperties was false, there was no status for it, and no field to state its limits. That blocked the whole observed-record path gated to v2.2. An otcs_observed edge is now required to carry both its non-claims and its sources; the schema refuses it otherwise.

v0.1.0 published — the first public release. Signed tag verified against SHA256:xYmRe0iaVZGTw77FEhx3Ez2/E6K28GL8EO9YuN8/FMM, the fingerprint now published in MAINTAINERS.md §1 alongside .allowed_signers, so any reader can verify the tag without trusting the forge. Ships the whole corpus at once: governance, coordinate vocabulary, 9 schemas + 3 wire schemas, 10 interfaces, 7 registry records (3 real, 4 example), and the tooling to verify it from a clean clone. Non-claims are in docs/releases/v0.1.0.md and are the longest section: no endorsement, no consensus, no proof the vocabulary is neutral or sufficient, and no ecosystem — 1 qualifying project and 1 steward, both the founder's.

Anchor round for v0.1.0 over four targets — the governance ledger, the registry tree digest, the measured roadmap status, and SHA256SUMS.hash, which commits the release artifact SET rather than only its members. Recorded after the round completed, because a manifest cannot commit the hash of a ledger that already contains the event describing it. Status is ANCHOR_PENDING: no OpenTimestamps client is installed, so the digests are fixed and stampable later. ANCHOR_PENDING must never be described as anchored — nothing here yet proves when these bytes existed.

OpenTimestamps client installed and all three manifests stamped. anchor-0001, anchor-0002 and anchor-0003 move from ANCHOR_PENDING to ANCHOR_SUBMITTED and now carry .ots proof files. ANCHOR_SUBMITTED is NOT a timestamp: calendar servers hold the hashes and intend to commit them to a future Bitcoin block, and that intention is not evidence. Nothing is proven about when these bytes existed until a block confirms, typically hours later, at which point npm run anchor:verify promotes the state to ANCHOR_CONFIRMED. Recorded now because the submission is a real event; described precisely because a Bitcoin proof carries an aura of finality far beyond what submission establishes.

A second independent witness now holds all three manifests. Rekor, the sigstore append-only transparency log, confirmed anchor-0001 through anchor-0003 on inclusion — the manifest is signed with the release key published in MAINTAINERS.md §1, so the log entry records who submitted which digest and when the log saw it. anchor-0003 covers the v0.1.0 release manifest. OpenTimestamps remains ANCHOR_SUBMITTED: four Bitcoin calendars hold the hashes and no block commits them yet, so Bitcoin still proves nothing about these bytes. The aggregate reads ANCHOR_CONFIRMED because one witness confirmed, which proves the bytes existed; it does not mean the record is independent of that witness, which is why the per-witness state is what gets published. The two fail differently on purpose — Bitcoin has no operator and takes hours, Rekor has an operator and is immediate.

Bitcoin has now confirmed. All three manifests carry BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation for blocks 960160, 960161 and 960164, so both registered witnesses are CONFIRMED and anchor-0003 — which covers the v0.1.0 release manifest — is externally witnessed twice by parties with unrelated failure domains. This is the first point at which anything in this repository is provably older than an assertion by its own maintainer. Two defects in the checking code were found doing this: ots verify writes to stderr, so a stdout-only capture silently never matched and CONFIRMED was unreachable; and ots verify requires a local Bitcoin node, which would have made confirmation depend on running a full node. Confirmation is now read from the proof itself via ots info, which needs no node and no network, and names the blocks so any reader can check the headers independently.

OTCS-0004 (model_revision) drafted: a registry entry is licensed by its author, not by the contribution licences. Found by a prospective registrant who asked for confirmation that a listing grants no rights beyond distributing the entry itself — confirmation the current documents could not honestly give, because DCO.md's two licence categories sweep a project's own otcs.yaml into CC BY 4.0 while PARTICIPATION.md promises no such grant is required, and the consent block asks for consent to five undefined scopes. Clock 45-90 days from 2026-07-31. Should ratify before any third party registers, while every affected record still belongs to the founder.

OTCS-0005 (model_revision) drafted: a SEALED evidence state - provably dated, deliberately undisclosed, never inflated. Four independent arrivals at the same missing state: the financial-crime profile (dual-use controls cannot evidence themselves), and three prospective registrants approaching from IP protection, architectural review, and commercial confidentiality. First model revision motivated primarily by external evidence. The state is constructed weaker-or-equal to disclosure on every axis except the one thing it proves: content with this hash existed by the witnessed time. Clock 45-90 days from 2026-07-31.

Publication model settled by the maintainer: below v1.0.0, published means the public repository and the signed tag — build in the open. Forge Release pages begin at v1.0.0. The v0.1.0 draft release object is retained unpublished as artifact storage, deliberately: the tarballs embed modification times, so a rebuild would not reproduce the byte-exact set whose SHA256SUMS.hash anchor-0003 attests in Bitcoin blocks 960160-960164 and the Rekor log. Deleting the draft would orphan the anchor's fourth target; keeping it unpublished keeps the proof resolvable without implying a finished product. VERSION_PUBLISHED (ev-000018) stands as recorded — the tag was and remains the publication.

OTCS-0003 received its first external exercise. A constitutional-runtime project with an explicit normative architecture - identity, purpose and constitutional authority preceding intelligence and execution - was mapped into the proposed three layers as a design test. Result: the project mapped while remaining recognisably itself. Its coordinates filled Layer 1 without renaming its native architecture; its explicit normativity landed in Layer 2 exactly because Layer 2 is declared free-text - an enum of normative goods would have distorted this project immediately, which strengthens the declared-never-enumerated rule rather than merely sparing it. Its eight native functions mapped into Layer 3 without replacement of its own vocabulary. The subject is not named: no consent to appear in this record, and the dry-run cannot enter the registry for the same reason. This is the foreign-architecture sovereignty criterion in rehearsal; passing it for real requires the steward to confirm, qualify or dispute.

OTCS-0006 (model_revision) drafted: project families - one project, several artifacts, honest counts. Two convergent sources: a design test in which a prospective subject with a constitution, standard, runtime and predecessor concepts would have become four or five records or one flattened one; and the registry's own first records, where ktp/ktp-demo/abt are already a family that only maintainer judgement keeps from counting as three. The family block is additive, carries no authority hierarchy, is never assigned by observation, and moves the one-body-of-work counting rule from judgement into structure. Measured count unchanged by design: 1 before, 1 after. Clock 45-90 days from 2026-07-31.

First analysis record published: a project_baseline for ktp under the new self-verification-attempt-v1 method. Honest result: KTP's own claims.yaml already recorded a negative result (independent second implementation sought, not achieved, SELF_ASSERTED, maturity 0); this analysis formalised it and found nothing that moves it forward - no second implementation exists anywhere to run the falsifier suite against, and no action available to the founder changes that. Building this artifact surfaced a real schema defect: analysis.schema.json required relationship_state on every finding unconditionally, which is meaningless for a single-subject project_baseline - the enum only has relationship values. Fixed by making it conditional on subjects.length >= 2, a requirement correction to an existing type, not a new capability, so it did not need a proposal. Satisfies published_failures_or_negative_results in the v1.0 gate.

First composition attempt published, and it failed - by design that is the point. Tested whether KTP's authorization model (an external decision point evaluating environment before an action proceeds) could wrap TCP congestion control. Result: NOT CURRENTLY COMPOSABLE. KTP presumes a place to intervene; TCP's calibration case already establishes it has none by design - authority empty, enforce 0.0, nothing external can refuse a send. A narrower reading (KTP consuming TCP's congestion state as an environment signal at a different, real enforcement point) was recorded as NOT_CURRENTLY_PROVABLE rather than refuted - blocked on missing implementation, not a structural mismatch. Both findings carry a skeptical review arguing the opposite conclusion. Satisfies published_non_composition in the sovereignty block. No composition schema was built for this - it is prose analysis under the existing analysis type, evidence toward a future design rather than a substitute for one.
Building it found two real schema defects. skeptical_review was required via a `contains` check at the array level, so one strong finding silently required skeptical_review on every finding in the set including weak ones with nothing to defend - rewritten as a genuine per-item conditional. And the earlier relationship_state fix's error-path label always said "projects" regardless of which directory actually failed; corrected to reflect the real path.

Lifecycle fixture: ownership transferred from Chris Perkins (individual) to Open Trust Commons (organisational steward), per PROJECT-LIFECYCLE.md §1. Recorded as a governance event, not a field edit - ownership_history and maintainership_transfers both carry the old and new owner with dates. Second step of a deliberate registered -> transferred -> corrected -> withdrawn exercise on a disclosed process fixture (registry/projects/ lifecycle-fixture), never a real project and structurally disqualified from every count.

Lifecycle fixture, third step: a genuine correction. coordinates and governed_object had been set only to satisfy schema minimums, not because the fixture actually governs anything - the exact confusion between "value present to satisfy the schema" and "value asserting something true" that EVIDENCE-MODEL.md §4b exists to name. Corrected as a new statement appended to known_limitations, record_version bumped to 3; the original text remains readable above it and in git history rather than being edited away.

Lifecycle fixture, fourth and final step: withdrawn. Completes registered (ev-000029 area) -> transferred (ev-000030) -> corrected (ev-000031) -> withdrawn, exercised end to end against real tooling rather than described in prose. Full history stays readable in the record and in this log; withdrawal ends participation, it does not retract anything. registry count correctly moved 3 registered -> 4 registered (transfer step) -> 3 registered again (withdrawal), confirming withdrawn records are excluded the same way example records are. Satisfies completed_provenance_lifecycles (evidence_and_interop) and correction_withdrawal_or_transfer_exercised (governance) in the v1.0 gate - both performed on a disclosed process fixture that could never count as a qualifying project, not on a real stakeholder, and both criteria's evidence says so plainly rather than implying more than was demonstrated.

Disaster recovery restoration tested for real, from zero. Fresh clone of the public remote into a machine with no prior state - no working directory, no node_modules, nothing cached. Ledger verified (32 events, chain intact), all records validated, both anchor witnesses re-confirmed from the fresh copy (proving the .ots and .sig proof files were actually pushed, not left local), and the site build reproduced byte-identically twice. Full account, including what was NOT tested (org deletion, key loss, archival-deposit restore - no DOI exists yet), recorded in INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md §9.
The exercise found a real gap rather than only confirming the happy path: the signing key exists in exactly one place, this machine, with no offline backup anywhere - despite INCIDENT-RESPONSE.md §1 committing to one, "verified at every release." Recorded as a finding, not silently fixed, because noting the promise as met without checking would be exactly the untested-backup problem the promise exists to prevent.
Satisfies disaster_recovery_restoration_tested in the v1.0 security block. key_rotation_tested remains separately unmet and is now informed by this finding.

Decided not to drill key rotation live right now, and recorded why rather than leaving the criterion silently unmet. Two reasons. First, sequencing: the 2026-08-01 DR exercise found no offline backup of the current signing key exists anywhere; rotating before a backup exists means a mistake mid-drill could lose signing entirely with nothing to recover from - backup has to come before rotation drills, not after. Second, the key's published fingerprint is already quoted in unsent draft replies to three prospective registrants; rotating it now would invalidate text nobody has seen yet for no operational reason, and rotating a maintainer's live published key is an irreversible, outward-facing action regardless.
key_rotation_tested stays unmet. The correct order is recorded in roadmap/releases/1.0.0.yaml: back up the current key offline first, then drill rotation for real.
